topics.title: Sorting and Classifying Objects
topics.concept:
What is sorting objects?

Sorting objects means putting things into groups based on how they are the same. When you sort, you look for things that share a special quality called a property.

What is classifying objects?

Classifying is a fancy word for sorting! When you classify, you decide which group each object belongs to. Scientists classify animals, teachers classify students by age, and you classify your toys by type!

Ways to sort objects:

PropertyExamplesGroups
ColourRed, blue, yellow blocksRed group, blue group, yellow group
ShapeCircles, squares, trianglesAll circles together, all squares together
SizeBig, medium, smallBig toys, small toys
UseEating, writing, playingFood group, stationery group, toy group
MaterialPlastic, wood, metalPlastic toys, wooden toys

Why do we sort and classify?

  • It helps us find things easily (like finding all red crayons)
  • It helps us count things faster
  • It helps us compare different groups
  • It is the first step to making graphs

examples.problem: Sort these fruits into two groups: 🍎 🍌 🍎 🍊 🍌 🍎
examples.solution:
• Look at all the fruits
  • Find fruits that are the same
  • Group 1 (Apples): 🍎 🍎 🍎 → 3 apples
  • Group 2 (Bananas): 🍌 🍌 → 2 bananas
  • Group 3 (Oranges): 🍊 → 1 orange
  • Three groups total

Answer: Apples: 3, Bananas: 2, Oranges: 1

• Identify all colours: Red (🔴) and Blue (🔵)
  • Red shapes: ■ (square), ● (circle), ▲ (triangle) → 3 red shapes
  • Blue shapes: ▲ (triangle), ■ (square) → 2 blue shapes
  • Red group has 3 shapes, Blue group has 2 shapes

Answer: Red: 3 shapes, Blue: 2 shapes

examples.problem: A toy box has 4 cars, 3 dolls, and 5 balls. If you sort by size, you find that 2 cars are big and 2 are small, 1 doll is big and 2 are small, and 3 balls are big and 2 are small. How many big toys are there in total? How many small toys?
examples.solution:
• Big cars: 2
  • Big dolls: 1
  • Big balls: 3
  • Total big toys = 2 + 1 + 3 = 6
  • Small cars: 2
  • Small dolls: 2
  • Small balls: 2
  • Total small toys = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6
  • Check: Total toys = 4+3+5=12, 6 big + 6 small = 12 ✓

Answer: 6 big toys, 6 small toys

recap: Sorting means putting things into groups that are the same
You can sort by colour, shape, size, use, or material
Sorting is the first step to making graphs
Different people might sort the same things in different ways!

topics.title: Picture Graphs and Tally Marks
topics.concept:
What is a picture graph?

A picture graph (or pictograph) uses pictures or symbols to show data. Each picture stands for a certain number of things. Picture graphs make it easy to see which group has the most or least.

What are tally marks?

Tally marks are a quick way to count and record numbers. You draw a line for each item. Every 5th mark crosses the first four, making it easy to count by 5s!

How to make tally marks:

NumberTally MarksHow to Write
1\One line
2\\Two lines
3\\\Three lines
4\\\\Four lines
5~~\\\\~~Four lines crossed by the fifth
6~~\\\\~~ \One group of 5 + 1
10~~\\\\~~ ~~\\\\~~Two groups of 5

How to read a picture graph:

  • Step 1: Look at the title to know what the graph is about
  • Step 2: Look at the key to see what each picture means
  • Step 3: Count the pictures in each row
  • Step 4: Compare the rows to answer questions

examples.problem: Count the tally marks: ~~\| \|\|\|~~ ~~\| \|\|\|~~ \|\| What number is this?

Look at this picture graph. Key: 🧸 = 1 toy. How many more cars than dolls?

Cars: 🚗 🚗 🚗 🚗 🚗 (5)

Dolls: 🎎 🎎 🎎 (3)
examples.solution:
• Count cars: 5 cars
  • Count dolls: 3 dolls
  • Difference: 5 - 3 = 2
  • Cars have 2 more than dolls

Answer: 2 more cars

examples.problem: A picture graph shows favourite pets. Key: 🐕 = 2 students. Dogs: 🐕 🐕 🐕, Cats: 🐕 🐕, Fish: 🐕. How many students chose dogs? How many total students?
examples.solution:
• Dogs: 3 pictures × 2 = 6 students
  • Cats: 2 pictures × 2 = 4 students
  • Fish: 1 picture × 2 = 2 students
  • Total students = 6 + 4 + 2 = 12 students

Answer: 6 students like dogs; 12 total students

recap: Picture graphs use pictures to show information
Every picture graph has a title and a key
The key tells you what each picture means
Tally marks help you count and record without writing numbers
Picture graphs make it easy to see which is most and which is least

topics.title: Simple Tables and Reading Information from Graphs
topics.concept:
What is a simple table?

A simple table is a way to organise data using rows and columns. Rows go across (left to right) and columns go up and down. Tables make information neat and easy to read!

What does reading information from graphs mean?

When you read information from a graph, you look at the pictures or data and answer questions like "How many?" "Which is most?" "How many more?" "What is the total?"

Parts of a table:

PartWhat it doesExample
TitleTells what the table is about"Our Favourite Colours"
RowA horizontal line of informationRed, Blue, Green
ColumnA vertical line of informationColour, Number
CellOne box in the tableThe number 5

How to read a table:

  • Step 1: Read the title to know what the table shows
  • Step 2: Look at the row and column labels
  • Step 3: Find the cell where the row and column meet
  • Step 4: Use the numbers to answer questions

Types of questions from graphs and tables:

Question TypeExampleHow to Find Answer
How many?How many like blue?Look at the number for blue
Which is most?Which colour is most liked?Find the largest number
Which is least?Which colour is least liked?Find the smallest number
How many more?How many more like red than blue?Subtract smaller from larger
TotalHow many children in total?Add all numbers together

examples.problem:
Look at this table. How many children like ice cream? How many like cake? Which is more popular?

DessertNumber of Children
Ice Cream12
Cake7
Cookies5
examples.solution:
• Ice cream: 12 children
  • Cake: 7 children
  • Compare: 12 is greater than 7
  • Ice cream is more popular (12 > 7)

Answer: Ice cream: 12, Cake: 7, Ice cream is more popular

examples.problem:
Use the picture graph to answer: How many total fruits? Key: 🍎 = 2 fruits

Apples: 🍎 🍎 🍎

Bananas: 🍎 🍎

Oranges: 🍎
examples.solution:
• Apples: 3 pictures × 2 = 6 fruits
  • Bananas: 2 pictures × 2 = 4 fruits
  • Oranges: 1 picture × 2 = 2 fruits
  • Total = 6 + 4 + 2 = 12 fruits

Answer: 12 fruits

examples.problem: The tally marks for favourite sports are: Cricket: ~~\| \|\|\|~~ ~~\| \|\|\|~~, Football: ~~\| \|\|\|~~ \|\|, Tennis: \|\|\|. How many more people like Cricket than Tennis? What is the total number of people?
examples.solution:
• Cricket: two groups of 5 = 10 people
  • Football: one group of 5 + 2 = 7 people
  • Tennis: 3 people
  • Cricket - Tennis = 10 - 3 = 7 more people like Cricket
  • Total = 10 + 7 + 3 = 20 people

Answer: 7 more like Cricket; 20 people total

recap: Tables organise data in rows and columns
Reading graphs means finding information from pictures or tables
Always look at the title first to know what the graph is about
For picture graphs, check the key to know what each picture means
Common questions: how many, which is most/least, how many more, total
Tables and graphs help us understand information quickly

questions.q: What is the tally mark for 7?
In a picture graph, key: 🍎 = 3 students. How many students if there are 4 🍎?
Which is the most in this table? Colour: Red(5), Blue(8), Green(3), Yellow(4)
How many more like Red (5) than Green (3)?
Sort by shape: ○, □, △, ○, □, △, ○. How many circles?
What is the total in this table? Dogs(4), Cats(5), Fish(2), Birds(3)
In a picture graph, 5 pictures of 🐕 with key 🐕 = 2 dogs. How many dogs?
Which is the least? Red(7), Blue(3), Green(6), Yellow(5)
A class collected data on eye colour: Brown: 12, Blue: 8, Green: 5, Black: 10. How many fewer children have brown eyes than the sum of green and black eyes?
questions.explanation: Green + Black = 5 + 10 = 15. Brown = 12. Difference = 15 - 12 = 3. So, brown eyes are 3 fewer.

questions.q: Tally marks are recorded for 5 days: Mon:5, Tue:7, Wed:4, Thu:9, Fri:6. What is the total of the two days with the highest and lowest values?

A picture graph shows fruit sales. Key: 🍎 = 5 fruits. Apples: 4 🍎, Bananas: 3 🍎, Oranges: 2 🍎, Grapes: 1 🍎. How many total fruits were sold? If oranges sold double, how many oranges would there be then?
questions.explanation: Apples = 20, Bananas = 15, Oranges = 10, Grapes = 5. Total = 20 + 15 + 10 + 5 = 50. Double of oranges = 20.

questions.q: A table shows: Monday-8, Tuesday-5, Wednesday-7, Thursday-?, Friday-6. The total for the week is 35. Find Thursday’s value. Also find how much greater Thursday is than the average of the other four days.
questions.explanation: Sum of known days = 8 + 5 + 7 + 6 = 26. Thursday = 35 - 26 = 9. Average of other four days = 26 ÷ 4 = 6.5. Difference = 9 - 6.5 = 2.5.
